title: Strategic Decision: System Rebuild Option

fields.headline: Three Options for System Recovery
fields.narration: The facilitator stands and addresses the group. 'The time for debate is over. We now have three options for recovering from this breach. Option A: 'Scorched Earth' — shut down every system, wipe every server, and rebuild from clean OS images. Estimated time: five to seven days. The airport operates entirely manually. Option B: 'Surgical Strike' — isolate and rebuild only the three confirmed compromised systems. Everything else stays online. But if other systems are infected and you don’t know it, the attacker could still move laterally. Option C: 'Monitor & Contain' — leave all systems running, deploy full network monitoring, and build a parallel clean network in the background. But if the attacker detects the monitoring, they may escalate immediately. The choice is yours. Make it now.'
keyFacts: Option A: Full shutdown and rebuild — 5–7 days; airport operates manually.
Option B: Rebuild only three systems — risk of undetected compromise elsewhere.
Option C: Monitor live systems — risk of attacker escalation if detected.
fields.expectedAction: Each team presents its recommendation. Ops leads the decision. No option is inherently correct — all carry operational and technical tradeoffs.
fields.facilitatorNote: Pause after the narration. Let the teams deliberate. Watch for whether any team defaults to Option A (scorched earth) out of fear, or Option C (monitor) out of overconfidence. The goal is not to reach consensus but to surface risk tolerance and communication gaps.

instructorNote: This inject is the decision point for Phase 4. The discussion will reveal team risk appetite, trust in systems, and coordination between technical and operational leadership. Watch for whether legal/HR concerns are raised, and whether any team suggests a fourth option.
